title: Economic Impacts of Climate Change in the United States: Integrating and Harmonizing Evidence from Recent Studies
abstract: arXiv:2509.00212v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This paper synthesizes evidence on climate change impacts specific to U.S. populations. We develop an apples-to-apples comparison of econometric studies that empirically estimate the relationship between climate change and gross domestic product (GDP). We demonstrate that with harmonized probabilistic socioeconomic and climate inputs these papers project a narrower and lower range of 2100 GDP losses than what is reported across the published studies, yet the implied U.S.-specific social cost of greenhouse gases (SC-GHG) is still greater than the market-based damage estimates in current enumerative models. We also take a first step in integrating evidence on nonmarket damages with the GDP impacts. Our findings highlight the need for more research addressing the limitations of macroeconomic empirical studies and research on nonmarket and international spillover impacts. translated_title: 美国气候变化的经济影响：整合与协调近期研究的证据
translated_abstract: 本文综合了针对美国人口的气候变化影响的证据。我们对实证估计气候变化与国内生产总值（GDP）之间关系的计量经济学研究进行了统一口径的比较。我们证明，在使用统一协调的概率性社会经济和气候输入条件下，这些论文预测的2100年GDP损失范围比已发表文献中所报告的范围更窄且更低，但由此隐含的美国特定的温室气体社会成本（SC-GHG）仍然高于当前列举式模型中基于市场的损害估计。我们还迈出了将非市场损害证据与GDP影响相整合的第一步。我们的发现强调了需要更多研究来解决宏观经济实证研究的局限性，以及关于非市场损害和国际溢出影响的研究。对于宏观经济方法与列举式方法如何……（原文截断）
tldr: 本文通过统一协调的输入条件对美国气候变化经济影响的计量经济学研究进行标准化比较，发现2100年GDP损失预测范围更窄且更低，但其隐含的温室气体社会成本仍高于现行列举式模型的市场损害估计，并首次尝试将非市场损害证据与GDP影响相整合。
